channel.title: Opal.Chien · Medical AI Notes (sample content)
channel.description: I'm Opal, a medical AI engineer. Notes on imaging research, model experiments, and the engineering work that turns ideas into systems.

item.title: From Model to Clinic: Engineering Beyond Training
item.description: [Sample article] Inference is one step. Inputs, outputs, error handling, and traceability turn a model into a system people can use.

item.title: Split Patients Before Images: The Basics of Data Partitioning
item.description: [Sample article] Examinations from the same patient may be more similar than expected. Establish independence before training.

item.title: A Mask's Position Matters as Much as Its Accuracy
item.description: [Sample article] Track spacing, orientation, and coordinate space from DICOM to NIfTI so segmentation stays aligned through conversion.

item.title: Leave Enough Behind to Reproduce the Next Training Run
item.description: [Sample article] A seed is only the beginning. Keep configurations, data splits, checkpoints, and experiment records together.

item.title: Beyond the Score: Keep the Cases That Went Wrong
item.description: [Sample article] AUC, Dice, and mAP are summaries. Case-level outputs reveal what an average cannot tell us.

item.title: Move Paths Out of Your Code: Start with a Configuration File
item.description: [Sample article] Centralize data locations, model weights, and output directories so the same program is easier to run elsewhere.

item.title: From Patch to Patient: Preserve the Links in MIL
item.description: [Sample article] Keep patch sources and positions alongside features so attention results can be mapped back to the original image.

item.title: A Place to Keep the Thoughts Behind the Work
item.description: [Sample article] Some things deserve to live beyond the terminal. Keep a record of questions, decisions, and lessons learned.
